bounds.domain: One persisted device approval and one dispatch attempt. Owner, digest, attempt and exact receipt equality are symbolic. The approval expiry boundary is a Boolean clock event.
bounds.abstraction: Claim and dispatch commit together before the permit. A lost reply or restart cannot create a new claim. A confirmed non-delivery record is retryable in the shared store and remains closed to device HTTP claim.
bounds.limits: The generic approval list is modeled only for exclusion of device approvals. Non-device execution, enrollment revocation, multiple proposals, transaction failures, provider effects and arbitrary receipt payloads remain separate.
bounds.conformance: Existing loopback HTTP and PGlite exercise the atomic dispatch mark, an applied receipt and repeat-claim denial. The real Photos service and PGlite exercise exact replay, foreign binding, wrong attempt and rejection after confirmed non-delivery. The broader device REST test covers the generic list and restart after dispatch.

assumptions: No fairness. The device claim and dispatch mark share a durable transaction.
No fairness. Only the device HTTP authority can act on this record.
No fairness. An invalid binding, attempt, expiry or transition grants no write.
Weak fairness of receiving and committing a valid device receipt. It may establish application or uncertainty.
Weak fairness of an authenticated owner confirming and committing the outcome of an uncertain dispatch.
No fairness. A dispatched device effect can remain unreported indefinitely.
